problem: What categorial relationship holds among determinatives (some, the) and established noun subcategories (common nouns, proper nouns, pronouns) in English — specifically, whether determinatives belong within Noun.
debate: The CGEL framework's analysis of English lexical categories (Huddleston & Pullum 2002), including its justification of pronouns within Noun and the auxiliary-within-Verb precedent (Pullum & Wilson 1977).
gap: CGEL excludes determinatives from Noun on the basis of their distinctive inflection and dependents, but its own logic for including pronouns despite comparable differences has not been extended to determinatives, and a matched comparison of their independent uses, partitives, modification and compounds is missing.
contribution: A D-noun analysis placing determinatives within Noun, extended via the same grounds CGEL uses for pronouns, supported by a matched comparison preserving lexical restrictions, plus a further ordinary-headedness proposal and a provisional four-way coordinate subcategorization.
note: The opening states a clear, well-scoped thesis against a specific framework with an explicit evidentiary strategy, though it must ultimately deliver the promised matched comparison; it warrants full review.
